Summary with SLOOS context:
- Macro tone stays mildly positive: solid job gains, unemployment near lows, inflation still below 2 percent, and policy remains accommodative with gradual normalization.
- SLOOS tempers the outlook: banks expect to ease standards for C&I and some residential mortgages (supportive), but expect tighter standards for CRE and construction, and for auto loans; banks expect deteriorating asset quality in credit cards and autos, while expecting improved C&I asset quality; foreign banks broadly expect to tighten C&I and CRE standards and report weaker business-loan demand.
- Net read: credit supply looks mixed—supportive for prime business and mortgage borrowing but tighter in riskier segments—helping explain soft business investment and posing headwinds for certain consumer/CRE categories. This slightly reduces the otherwise positive tone.
